completion_data.completion_summary: Closed task 621 as a verification pass over the already-built typescript extension: re-confirmed the baseline (20 files, 9/9 index-entries.json line counts, 4 parity-plus manifest items, 5 lints) had not drifted, executed the dispatch's VERIFICATION clause end-to-end against a disposable scratch target (all four merge targets confirmed, including the opencode.json.managed gating behavior), and extended the extension's own README with the durable verification procedure.

memory_candidates.content: The opencode_json merge target is gated by a .managed marker file: merge.lua's generate_opencode_json (Step 1.2) returns ok=true and writes nothing unless <target>/opencode.json.managed exists. End-to-end verification of a new extension's four merge targets via a headless scratch-target manager.load(name, {confirm=false, force=true, project_dir=SCRATCH}) must create that marker before the opencode_json target can be observed at all; a tester who does not know this will misread a correctly gated no-op as a broken merge target. Now documented in agent-system/extensions/typescript/README.md's Verification section as a reusable worked example.

verify-deploy.sh's per-gate check-extension-docs.sh (gate 3) rolls up ALL extensions into one aggregate PASS/FAIL; a single unrelated extension's pre-existing drift (e.g. a stale index-entries.json line_count) fails the whole gate even when the extension actually under test is fine. When using --only-gate to scope a Batch Gate Deferral discharge, verify the NAMED extension's own per-extension row/table entry directly rather than trusting the gate's aggregate exit code, and record any unrelated failing extension as a separate out-of-scope issue rather than treating it as blocking.
